modules.title: Introduction to Military Rule in Nigeria
modules.html:
The coups of 1966 and later military regimes, their policies and the return to civil rule. This section covers introduction to military rule in nigeria.

Key points

  • Nigeria's return to civil rule on May 29, 1999, ended the military regime of _____. — Abdulsalami Abubakar.
  • The strategy of 'Indirect Rule' was most successful in the _____ of Nigeria. — Northern Region.
  • The Indirect Rule system failed in Southeastern Nigeria primarily because _____. — there were no centralized traditional rulers like Emirs.
  • The Indirect Rule system was most successful in the _____ part of Nigeria. — Northern.
  • The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on _____. — January 15, 1966.

Worked examples

Q: Nigeria's return to civil rule on May 29, 1999, ended the military regime of _____.
A: Abdulsalami Abubakar — General Abubakar oversaw the transition to the Fourth Republic after Abacha's death.

Q: The strategy of 'Indirect Rule' was most successful in the _____ of Nigeria.
A: Northern Region — Indirect Rule worked best in the North because of the existing centralized political structure of the Sokoto Caliphate and the Emirate system.

examples.q: Nigeria's return to civil rule on May 29, 1999, ended the military regime of _____.
The strategy of 'Indirect Rule' was most successful in the _____ of Nigeria.

quiz.q: Nigeria's return to civil rule on May 29, 1999, ended the military regime of _____.
quiz.solution: General Abubakar oversaw the transition to the Fourth Republic after Abacha's death.

quiz.q: The strategy of 'Indirect Rule' was most successful in the _____ of Nigeria.
quiz.solution: Indirect Rule worked best in the North because of the existing centralized political structure of the Sokoto Caliphate and the Emirate system.

quiz.q: The Indirect Rule system failed in Southeastern Nigeria primarily because _____.
options: there were no centralized traditional rulers like Emirs
quiz.solution: The decentralized nature of Igbo society (acephalous) meant that the British creation of 'Warrant Chiefs' was artificial and lacked traditional legitimacy.

quiz.q: The Indirect Rule system was most successful in the _____ part of Nigeria.
quiz.solution: Indirect Rule worked well in the North because of the pre-existing centralized emirate system of the Sokoto Caliphate.

quiz.q: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on _____.
quiz.solution: The January 1966 coup, led by Major Nzeogwu and others, ended the First Republic.

quiz.q: The first military coup in Nigeria was led by:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Major Kaduna Nzeogwu.

quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: The traditional system was decentralized (Acephalous).
